### Helper functions

In addition to the information above, I am running the following
functions for doing the following tasks:

-   extracting the legend for multipanel plots made

-   pooling correlations (since statistics presented will be from the
    pooled 20 datasets)

-   adding significance stars to exported tables (\*\*\* for p \< 0.001,
    \*\* for p \< 0.01, and \* for p \< 0.1, using an alpha of 0.1 to
    reflect our significance level since outputs will be 2 and 3-way
    interactions that require more statistical power)

-   formatting the pooled model outputs as estimate(stars if
    present)(90% lower bound, 90% upper bound)

-   calculating the pooled stats by treatment group for power analyses

```{r}
#| label: extract-legend-from-a-ggplot-as-a-standa
# extract legend from a ggplot as a standalone panel (used in multi-panel figures)
make_legend_panel <- function(plot_obj) {
  tmp <- plot_obj + 
    guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 1), shape = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
          legend.title = element_blank(),
          legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"),
          legend.spacing.y = unit(0.1, "cm"))
  legend_grob <- cowplot::get_legend(tmp)
  cowplot::ggdraw(legend_grob)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: pool-correlations-using-fisher-s-z-trans
# pool correlations using Fisher's z transformation (standard approach)
pool_correlations <- function(imp_data, var1, var2, m = 20) {
  r_vals <- sapply(1:m, function(i) {
    d <- imp_data %>% filter(.imp == i) %>% select(all_of(c(var1, var2)))
    cor(d[[var1]], d[[var2]], use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")
  })
  z_vals <- atanh(r_vals)
  pooled_z <- mean(z_vals)
  pooled_r <- tanh(pooled_z)
  pooled_r
}
```

```{r}
#| label: helper-functions-1
pool_correlations_spearman <- function(imp_data, var1, var2, m = 20) {
  r_vals <- sapply(1:m, function(i) {
    d <- imp_data %>% filter(.imp == i) %>% select(all_of(c(var1, var2)))
    cor(d[[var1]], d[[var2]], use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman")
  })
  z_vals <- atanh(r_vals)
  pooled_z <- mean(z_vals)
  tanh(pooled_z)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: significance-stars-for-formatted-tables
# significance stars for formatted tables
add_stars <- function(p) {
  case_when(
    p < 0.001 ~ "***",
    p < 0.01  ~ "**",
    p < 0.1   ~ "*",
    TRUE      ~ ""
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: format-pooled-model-result-as-estimate-l
# format pooled model result as "estimate** (lower, upper)" for export tables
format_result <- function(pooled_model, term_name) {
  s <- summary(pooled_model, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>%
    filter(term == term_name)
  if (nrow(s) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  stars <- add_stars(s$p.value)
  sprintf("%s%s (%.3f, %.3f)",
          formatC(round(s$estimate, 3), format = "f", digits = 3),
          stars,
          s$`5 %`,
          s$`95 %`)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: compute-pooled-stats-n-mean-sd-by-treatm
# compute pooled stats (n, mean, sd) by treatment group for power analyses
compute_power_stats <- function(outcome_var, data) {
  data %>%
    filter(.imp > 0) %>%
    group_by(.imp, family_3plus) %>%
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      mean_val = mean(.data[[outcome_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_val = sd(.data[[outcome_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    group_by(family_3plus) %>%
    summarise(
      pooled_n = mean(n),
      pooled_mean = mean(mean_val),
      pooled_sd = sqrt(mean(sd_val^2) + var(mean_val) * (1 + 1/20)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
```

### Data prep (pre-analysis)

The last step of data prep (one that needed to be done after imputation
for all the data to be available) is excluding all the 2017 births in
the 3+ children group. This is because we don't know whether they would
have been born before or after the cutoff date for the policy, meaning
that we can't know for sure whether they would have been affected by the
policy. To do so, I temporarily convert back to long form and filter
before converting back to a `mids` object.

```{r}
#| label: filter-out-2017-births-in-3-children-gro
# filter out 2017 births in 3+ children group for main analysis
imp_long_no2017 <- complete(imp_complete, "long", include = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!(family_3plus == 1 & third_child_yob == 2017))
```

```{r}
#| label: convert-back-to-mids
# convert back to mids
imp_no2017 <- as.mids(imp_long_no2017)
```

From this, we also create a couple of specific `mids` objects:

-   one is an interrupted time series-specific (ITS) object called
    `imp_long_its`, as this ITS analysis only uses the 3+ children group

-   one is a parallel time trends object that only contains information
    from time periods 1 (2009-2012) and 2 (2013-2016) in order to later
    verify whether the parallel trends assumption holds for DiD/CITS
    analyses

```{r}
#| label: create-its-specific-mids-object-3-famili
# create ITS-specific mids object (3+ families only) - this one works because family_3plus is not imputed
imp_long_its <- imp_long_no2017 %>%
  filter(family_3plus == 1)
imp_its <- as.mids(imp_long_its)
```

```{r}
#| label: create-parallel-trends-mids-object-bucke
# create parallel trends mids object (buckets 1-2 only) - this works because time_bucket is not imputed
imp_long_pt <- imp_long_no2017 %>%
  filter(time_bucket %in% c(1, 2))
imp_pt <- as.mids(imp_long_pt)
```

## Descriptives (for full dataset, including 2017 data)

The first step of analysis is obtaining descriptives - and these will
include for the full dataset, including individuals from 2017. For all
descriptives and analyses, these will be pooled values across all 20
imputed datasets.

The first set of descriptives I am obtaining will be Ns of each category
(in this case, `treated` refers to being affected by the rollout of the
two-child benefit cap, i.e. your 3rd child was born after the cutoff).

First are Ns for families:

```{r}
#| label: table-1a-sample-sizes-ns-treated-family
# table 1a: sample sizes, Ns treated (FAMILY-LEVEL counts) - pooled
family_level_table <- imp_long_full %>%
  filter(.imp > 0) %>%
  group_by(.imp, hidp, intyear) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    group_1_2           = (family_3plus == 0),
    group_3plus         = (family_3plus == 1 & (intyear < 2017 | is.na(treated))),
    group_3plus_treated = (family_3plus == 1 & intyear >= 2017 & !is.na(treated) & treated == 1)
  ) %>%
  group_by(.imp, intyear) %>%
  summarise(
    families_1_2           = sum(group_1_2, na.rm = TRUE),
    families_3plus         = sum(group_3plus, na.rm = TRUE),
    families_3plus_treated = sum(group_3plus_treated, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(intyear) %>%
  summarise(
    f_1_2    = round(mean(families_1_2)),
    f_3plus  = round(mean(families_3plus)),
    f_treated = round(mean(families_3plus_treated)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `Families 1-2 kids` = f_1_2,
    `Families 3+ kids`  = ifelse(f_3plus == 0, NA_real_, f_3plus),
    `Families 3+ treated (only post 2017), out of total` = ifelse(intyear < 2017, NA_real_, f_treated)
  ) %>%
  select(intyear, `Families 1-2 kids`, `Families 3+ kids`,
         `Families 3+ treated (only post 2017), out of total`) %>%
  rename(Year = intyear)
```

Then, obtaining Ns of individuals:

```{r}
#| label: table-1a-sample-sizes-ns-treated-individ
# table 1a: sample sizes, Ns treated (INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL counts) - pooled
individual_level_table <- imp_long_full %>%
  filter(.imp > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    group_1_2           = (family_3plus == 0),
    group_3plus         = (family_3plus == 1 & (intyear < 2017 | is.na(treated))),
    group_3plus_treated = (family_3plus == 1 & intyear >= 2017 & !is.na(treated) & treated == 1)
  ) %>%
  group_by(.imp, intyear) %>%
  summarise(
    individuals_1_2           = sum(group_1_2, na.rm = TRUE),
    individuals_3plus         = sum(group_3plus, na.rm = TRUE),
    individuals_3plus_treated = sum(group_3plus_treated, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(intyear) %>%
  summarise(
    i_1_2    = round(mean(individuals_1_2)),
    i_3plus  = round(mean(individuals_3plus)),
    i_treated = round(mean(individuals_3plus_treated)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `Individuals 1-2 kids` = i_1_2,
    `Individuals 3+ kids`  = ifelse(i_3plus == 0, NA_real_, i_3plus),
    `Individuals 3+ treated (only post 2017), out of total` = ifelse(intyear < 2017, NA_real_, i_treated)
  ) %>%
  select(intyear, `Individuals 1-2 kids`, `Individuals 3+ kids`,
         `Individuals 3+ treated (only post 2017), out of total`) %>%
  rename(Year = intyear)
```

Also, to obtain specific information on the proportion of affected
individuals per year (after the policy was implemented) from the 3+
children group (because they are only considered "affected" if their
third child was born after the two-child benefit cap was implemented) -
noting that I am using interview year here as a proxy because we don't
have information on month/day for birth:

```{r}
#| label: table-1a-supplement-proportion-of-treate
# table 1a (supplement): proportion of treated individuals within the 3+ children group by year
treated_proportions <- imp_long_full %>%
  filter(.imp > 0, family_3plus == 1, intyear >= 2018) %>%
  group_by(.imp, intyear) %>%
  summarise(
    n_total   = n(),
    n_treated = sum(treated == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(intyear) %>%
  summarise(
    pooled_total   = round(mean(n_total)),
    pooled_treated = round(mean(n_treated)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_treated = round(pooled_treated / pooled_total * 100, 1)
  ) %>%
  rename(Year = intyear)
```

These are total Ns for individuals and households by group (not by year,
as done above).

```{r}
#| label: table-1b-overall-n-individuals-and-house
# table 1b: overall N individuals and households by group (pooled across imputations)
group_ns <- imp_long_full %>%
  filter(.imp > 0) %>%
  mutate(group = ifelse(family_3plus == 0, "Control (1-2 children)", "Treatment (3+ children)")) %>%
  group_by(.imp, group) %>%
  summarise(
    n_individuals = n_distinct(pidp),
    n_households  = n_distinct(hidp),
    n_obs         = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(
    `N Individuals (unique)`  = round(mean(n_individuals)),
    `N Households (unique)`   = round(mean(n_households)),
    `N Observations (person-years)` = round(mean(n_obs)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

The next steps will involve obtaining information on confounders - both
the continuous and categorical ones, as well as the income quintiles -
for the descriptives table.

```{r}
#| label: table-1c-sample-characteristics-control
# table 1c: sample characteristics - control (1-2 children) vs treatment (3+ children) - pooled
covariates_continuous  <- c("age", "equiv_yearly")
covariates_categorical <- c("sex", "ethn_binary", "ukborn", "urban", "edu_qual",
                            "marstat", "oc_current", "chron_health")
```

```{r}
#| label: continuous-covariates-pooled-means-and-s
# continuous covariates - pooled means and SDs
covariate_continuous_pooled <- imp_long_full %>%
  filter(.imp > 0) %>%
  select(.imp, family_3plus, all_of(covariates_continuous)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(covariates_continuous), names_to = "covariate", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(.imp, family_3plus, covariate) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_val   = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(family_3plus, covariate) %>%
  summarise(
    pooled_mean = mean(mean_val),
    pooled_sd   = sqrt(mean(sd_val^2) + var(mean_val) * (1 + 1/20)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    result = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", pooled_mean, pooled_sd),
    group  = ifelse(family_3plus == 0, "Control (1-2 children)", "Treatment (3+ children)")
  ) %>%
  select(covariate, group, result) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = result)
```

```{r}
#| label: categorical-covariates-pooled-proportion
# categorical covariates - pooled proportions
covariate_categorical_pooled <- imp_long_full %>%
  filter(.imp > 0) %>%
  select(.imp, family_3plus, all_of(covariates_categorical)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(covariates_categorical), names_to = "covariate", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(.imp, family_3plus, covariate, value) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(.imp, family_3plus, covariate) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(family_3plus, covariate, value) %>%
  summarise(
    pooled_prop = mean(prop),
    pooled_n    = mean(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    result          = sprintf("%.0f (%.1f%%)", pooled_n, pooled_prop * 100),
    group           = ifelse(family_3plus == 0, "Control (1-2 children)", "Treatment (3+ children)"),
    covariate_level = paste0(covariate, "_", value)
  ) %>%
  select(covariate_level, group, result) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = result)
```

```{r}
#| label: income-quintiles-pooled-proportions
# income quintiles - pooled proportions
income_quintile_pooled <- imp_long_full %>%
  filter(.imp > 0) %>%
  mutate(income_quintile_label = case_when(
    income_quintile == 1 ~ "Income quintile 1 (Lowest)",
    income_quintile == 2 ~ "Income quintile 2",
    income_quintile == 3 ~ "Income quintile 3",
    income_quintile == 4 ~ "Income quintile 4",
    income_quintile == 5 ~ "Income quintile 5 (Highest)",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>%
  group_by(.imp, family_3plus, income_quintile_label) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(.imp, family_3plus) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(family_3plus, income_quintile_label) %>%
  summarise(
    pooled_prop = mean(prop),
    pooled_n    = mean(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(income_quintile_label)) %>%
  mutate(
    result   = sprintf("%.0f (%.1f%%)", pooled_n, pooled_prop * 100),
    group    = ifelse(family_3plus == 0, "Control (1-2 children)", "Treatment (3+ children)"),
    variable = income_quintile_label
  ) %>%
  select(variable, group, result) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = result)
```

```{r}
#| label: combine-continuous-categorical-and-incom
# combine continuous, categorical, and income quintiles
sample_characteristics_table <- bind_rows(
  covariate_continuous_pooled %>% rename(variable = covariate),
  covariate_categorical_pooled %>% rename(variable = covariate_level),
  income_quintile_pooled
)
```

This is additionally supplemented by information on descriptives for
each outcome by group.

```{r}
#| label: table-1d-outcome-descriptives-by-group-p
# table 1d: outcome descriptives by group (pooled means, SDs, observed range, N obs)
outcome_descriptives <- imp_long_full %>%
  filter(.imp > 0) %>%
  mutate(group = ifelse(family_3plus == 0, "Control (1-2 children)", "Treatment (3+ children)")) %>%
  select(.imp, group, all_of(outcomes_raw)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(outcomes_raw), names_to = "outcome", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(.imp, group, outcome) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_val   = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_val  = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_val  = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_obs    = sum(!is.na(value)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(group, outcome) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean  = round(mean(mean_val), 2),
    SD    = round(sqrt(mean(sd_val^2) + var(mean_val) * (1 + 1/20)), 2),
    Min   = round(mean(min_val), 2),
    Max   = round(mean(max_val), 2),
    N_obs = round(mean(n_obs)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(outcome = factor(outcome, levels = outcomes_raw, labels = outcome_labels)) %>%
  arrange(outcome, group)
```

Finally, we wanted to obtain means of all the outcomes by interview year
and group:

```{r}
#| label: table-2-means-90-cis-of-key-outcomes-by
# table 2: means (90% CIs) of key outcomes by group and year - pooled
outcome_means_by_year_pooled <- imp_long_full %>%
  filter(.imp > 0) %>%
  mutate(group = case_when(
    family_3plus == 0 ~ "1-2 children",
    family_3plus == 1 & post_policy_month == 0 ~ "3+ children",
    family_3plus == 1 & post_policy_month == 1 & intyear == 2017 & treated == 1  ~ "3+ children (treated)",
    family_3plus == 1 & post_policy_month == 1 & intyear == 2017 & is.na(treated) ~ "3+ children (unaffected)",
    family_3plus == 1 & post_policy_month == 1 & intyear == 2017 ~ "3+ children (pre-policy)",
    family_3plus == 1 & post_policy_month == 1 & intyear >= 2018 & treated == 1  ~ "3+ children (treated)",
    family_3plus == 1 & post_policy_month == 1 & intyear >= 2018 & is.na(treated) ~ "3+ children (unaffected)",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>%
  filter(!is.na(group)) %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c(
    "1-2 children", "3+ children", "3+ children (pre-policy)",
    "3+ children (treated)", "3+ children (unaffected)"
  ))) %>%
  # pivot to long for cleaner pooling
  select(.imp, intyear, group, all_of(outcomes_raw)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(outcomes_raw), names_to = "outcome", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(.imp, intyear, group, outcome) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_val   = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_val    = sum(!is.na(value)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(intyear, group, outcome) %>%
  summarise(
    pooled_mean = mean(mean_val),
    pooled_sd   = sqrt(mean(sd_val^2) + var(mean_val) * (1 + 1/20)),
    pooled_n    = mean(n_val),
    pooled_se   = pooled_sd / sqrt(pooled_n),
    ci_lower    = pooled_mean - 1.645 * pooled_se,
    ci_upper    = pooled_mean + 1.645 * pooled_se,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    result  = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f - %.2f)", pooled_mean, ci_lower, ci_upper),
    outcome = factor(outcome, levels = outcomes_raw, labels = outcome_labels)
  ) %>%
  select(intyear, group, outcome, result) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = outcome, values_from = result) %>%
  arrange(intyear, group) %>%
  rename(Year = intyear, Group = group)
```


## Correlation analyses

For this section, I will be generating correlation matrices for all of
the outcomes, just to obtain some idea as to how related the outcomes
might be (this is especially relevant for the HRQoL and self-rated
health outcomes, as the self-rated health question is the first question
of the HRQoL measure.)

Once again, this is pooled across 20 imputed datasets.

### General correlation matrix

```{r}
#| label: figure-correlation-matrix-numerical-for
# figure: correlation matrix (numerical) for all 7 outcomes - pooled
outcome_cor_data <- imp_long_full %>%
  filter(.imp > 0) %>%
  group_by(.imp) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(outcomes_raw), mean, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
#| label: pooled-correlation-matrix-across-imputat
# pooled correlation matrix across imputations
cor_matrices <- lapply(1:20, function(i) {
  imp_long_full %>%
    filter(.imp == i) %>%
    select(all_of(outcomes_raw)) %>%
    cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
})
pooled_cor_matrix <- Reduce("+", cor_matrices) / 20
colnames(pooled_cor_matrix) <- outcome_labels
rownames(pooled_cor_matrix) <- outcome_labels
```

```{r}
#| label: export-numerical-correlation-matrix-to-e
# export numerical correlation matrix to excel
wb_cor <- createWorkbook()
addWorksheet(wb_cor, "Correlation_Matrix")
writeData(wb_cor, "Correlation_Matrix",
          as.data.frame(round(pooled_cor_matrix, 3)),
          rowNames = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: figure-correlogram-for-all-7-outcomes
# figure: correlogram for all 7 outcomes
pooled_cor_matrix_ordered <- pooled_cor_matrix[display_order, display_order]
colnames(pooled_cor_matrix_ordered) <- outcome_labels_figures[display_order]
rownames(pooled_cor_matrix_ordered) <- outcome_labels_figures[display_order]
pdf("output/figure_correlogram_outcomes.pdf", width = 8, height = 7)
corrplot(pooled_cor_matrix_ordered,
         method      = "color",
         type        = "upper",
         tl.col      = "black",
         tl.srt      = 45,
         addCoef.col = "black",
         number.cex  = 0.8,
         col         = colorRampPalette(c("#D55E00", "white", "#0072B2"))(200),
         title       = "Pooled outcome correlations (across 20 imputations)",
         mar         = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
dev.off()
```

### Outcome correlations with `sex` and `income_quintile`

For these, I am not generating a figure, but I wanted to check these
correlations divided by sex and income quintile to see any variation in
these relevant demographics.

-   sex is binary (1 = male, 2 = female) - treated as numeric for
    point-biserial

-   income_quintile is ordinal (1-5) - treated as numeric (Spearman more
    appropriate)

Both approaches pool r across 20 imputations.

```{r}
#| label: 2a-pearson-correlations-outcomes-x-sex
# --- 2a: Pearson correlations: outcomes x sex ---
# sex is coded 1/2 so Pearson correlation is equivalent to point-biserial
sex_cors_pearson <- sapply(outcomes_raw, function(outcome) {
  pool_correlations(imp_long_full %>% filter(.imp > 0), outcome, "sex")
})
names(sex_cors_pearson) <- outcome_labels
# --- 2b: Pearson correlations: outcomes x income_quintile ---
income_cors_pearson <- sapply(outcomes_raw, function(outcome) {
  pool_correlations(imp_long_full %>% filter(.imp > 0), outcome, "income_quintile")
})
names(income_cors_pearson) <- outcome_labels
# --- 2c: Spearman correlations: outcomes x sex (robustness) ---
sex_cors_spearman <- sapply(outcomes_raw, function(outcome) {
  pool_correlations_spearman(imp_long_full %>% filter(.imp > 0), outcome, "sex")
})
names(sex_cors_spearman) <- outcome_labels
# --- 2d: Spearman correlations: outcomes x income_quintile (robustness) ---
income_cors_spearman <- sapply(outcomes_raw, function(outcome) {
  pool_correlations_spearman(imp_long_full %>% filter(.imp > 0), outcome, "income_quintile")
})
names(income_cors_spearman) <- outcome_labels
# --- 2e: assemble summary table ---
cor_with_demographics <- data.frame(
  Outcome                    = outcome_labels,
  r_sex_pearson              = round(sex_cors_pearson, 3),
  r_sex_spearman             = round(sex_cors_spearman, 3),
  r_income_quintile_pearson  = round(income_cors_pearson, 3),
  r_income_quintile_spearman = round(income_cors_spearman, 3),
  row.names = NULL
)
```

```{r}
#| label: export-to-existing-workbook
# export to existing workbook
addWorksheet(wb_cor, "Outcome_x_Demographics")
writeData(wb_cor, "Outcome_x_Demographics", cor_with_demographics)
# note on coding direction for interpretation
writeData(wb_cor, "Outcome_x_Demographics",
          data.frame(Note = c(
            "sex: 1 = male, 2 = female. Positive r = higher scores in females.",
            "income_quintile: 1 = lowest, 5 = highest. Positive r = higher scores in higher income groups.",
            "Pearson r used as primary; Spearman provided as robustness check for ordinal income variable.",
            "Correlations pooled across 20 imputations using Fisher z-transformation."
          )),
          startRow = nrow(cor_with_demographics) + 3)
# save updated workbook
saveWorkbook(wb_cor, "output/Correlation_Matrix_20260320.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

## Power analysis

For this section, I will be calcuating minimum detectable effects (MDEs)
for each outcome (see Section 4 setup section above for which label
corresponds to each outcome) at the α = 0.05 and α = 0.1 levels. This
gives, based on the Ns used for each type of analysis below (which will
be delineated), at 80% power, what the minimum effect is that we could
detect, in raw point estimates and standardised units.

In addition to these calculations, these chunks calculate sample
details, and then all results from the section are exported into an
Excel workbook.

```{r}
#| label: power-analysis-1
outcomes_raw <- c("GHQ_total", "SF_total", "general_health", "health_sat", "life_sat", "finnow", "finfut")
outcome_labels <- c("GHQ-12", "SF-12", "General Health", "Health Sat", "Life Sat", "Fin Now", "Fin Future")
```

```{r}
#| label: power-analysis-2
power_results <- map_dfr(seq_along(outcomes_raw), function(j) {
  outcome <- outcomes_raw[j]
  label   <- outcome_labels[j]
```

```{r}
#| label: power-analysis-3
  pd <- compute_power_stats(outcome, imp_long_no2017)
  n_ctrl <- pd %>% filter(family_3plus == 0) %>% pull(pooled_n)
  n_trt  <- pd %>% filter(family_3plus == 1) %>% pull(pooled_n)
  p_sd   <- mean(pd$pooled_sd)
```

```{r}
#| label: power-analysis-4
  its_05  <- pwr.t.test(n = n_trt, power = 0.80, sig.level = 0.05, type = "one.sample")
  its_10  <- pwr.t.test(n = n_trt, power = 0.80, sig.level = 0.10, type = "one.sample")
  did_05  <- pwr.t2n.test(n1 = n_trt, n2 = n_ctrl, power = 0.80, sig.level = 0.05)
  did_10  <- pwr.t2n.test(n1 = n_trt, n2 = n_ctrl, power = 0.80, sig.level = 0.10)
  cits_05 <- pwr.t.test(n = n_ctrl + n_trt, power = 0.80, sig.level = 0.05, type = "two.sample")
  cits_10 <- pwr.t.test(n = n_ctrl + n_trt, power = 0.80, sig.level = 0.10, type = "two.sample")
```

```{r}
#| label: power-analysis-5
  data.frame(
    Outcome              = label,
    Analysis             = rep(c("ITS", "DiD", "CITS"), each = 2),
    Alpha                = rep(c(0.05, 0.10), 3),
    Power                = 0.80,
    N_Treatment          = rep(c(n_trt, n_trt, n_trt), each = 2),
    N_Control            = rep(c(NA, n_ctrl, n_ctrl), each = 2),
    Pooled_SD            = p_sd,
    MDE_Cohen_d          = c(its_05$d, its_10$d, did_05$d, did_10$d, cits_05$d, cits_10$d),
    MDE_Raw              = c(its_05$d, its_10$d, did_05$d, did_10$d, cits_05$d, cits_10$d) * p_sd
  )
})
```

```{r}
#| label: sample-details-for-all-outcomes
# sample details for all outcomes
sample_details <- map_dfr(seq_along(outcomes_raw), function(j) {
  pd <- compute_power_stats(outcomes_raw[j], imp_long_no2017)
  pd %>%
    mutate(
      Outcome = outcome_labels[j],
      Group = ifelse(family_3plus == 0, "Control (1-2 children)", "Treatment (3+ children)")
    ) %>%
    select(Outcome, Group, N = pooled_n, Mean = pooled_mean, SD = pooled_sd)
})
```

```{r}
#| label: power-analysis-6
wb_power <- createWorkbook()
addWorksheet(wb_power, "Power_Analysis")
writeData(wb_power, "Power_Analysis", power_results)
addWorksheet(wb_power, "Sample_Details")
writeData(wb_power, "Sample_Details", sample_details)
saveWorkbook(wb_power, "output/Power_Analysis_20260320.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

## Interrupted time series (ITS) analyses

For interrupted time series analyses, I'm running unadjsted, adjusted,
and standardised (z-score) adjusted models for each outcome. These
models will be pooled over the 20 datasets and run for the full model,
as well as subgroup analyses for sex (male/female), ethnicity
(white/ethnic minority), and income quintile (bottom 3/top 2).

### Full models

#### Unadjusted (raw)

**Psychological distress**
```{r}
#| label: its-ghq-total
# GHQ_total
its_GHQ_full_unadj <- lapply(1:imp_its$m, function(i) {
  feols(GHQ_total ~ time_since_policy + post_policy_month + time_since_policy:post_policy_month,
        data = complete(imp_its, i),
        cluster = ~hidp)
})
class(its_GHQ_full_unadj) <- c("mira", "list")
its_GHQ_full_unadj_pooled <- pool(its_GHQ_full_unadj)
summary(its_GHQ_full_unadj_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90)
```

#### Adjusted (raw)

As a refresher, this includes the following confounders after
imputation:

-   age (`age`)

-   sex (`sex`)

-   ethnicity (`ethn_binary`)

-   country of birth (`ukborn`)

-   urbanicity (`urban`)

-   highest education level (`edu_qual`)

-   de facto marital status (`marstat`)

-   household income (`equiv_yearly`)

-   current occupation class (`oc_current`)

-   chronic health condition (`chron_health`)

**Psychological distress**

### Subgroup analyses

For all subgroup analyses, I am running them on standardised adjusted
models for two reasons: 1) these are the most comprehensive models, and
2) for simplicity's sake, as running subgroup analyses on all the models
run above would mean there are hundreds more models that are anyway less
specific.

### Data exporting

#### Generating figures

First, running some helper functions that will help with running the
tasks. These do the following:

For generating figures with predicted marginal means for all seven
outcomes:

-   building pooled observed means for an outcome

-   computing confounder means from ITS data in order to generate
    predicted marginal means

-   making the ITS panels with predicted marginal means

```{r}
#| label: its-figure-generation
## ITS figures — predicted marginal means, all 7 outcomes ----

# helper: build pooled observed means for one outcome (3+ families only)
# (this is unchanged from before)
build_its_plot_data <- function(outcome_var, data_long) {
  data_long %>%
    filter(.imp > 0, family_3plus == 1) %>%
    group_by(.imp, intyear) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_val = mean(.data[[outcome_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    group_by(intyear) %>%
    summarise(
      pooled_mean = mean(mean_val),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(intyear != 2017) %>%
    mutate(post = as.integer(intyear > 2017))
}

# helper: compute covariate means from the ITS data for predicted marginal means
compute_covariate_contribution <- function(pooled_model, imp_data_long) {
  # get all covariate coefficient names (exclude ITS terms and intercept)
  its_terms <- c("(Intercept)", "time_since_policy", "post_policy_month", 
                 "time_since_policy:post_policy_month")
  all_coefs <- summary(pooled_model) %>% select(term, estimate)
  cov_coefs <- all_coefs %>% filter(!term %in% its_terms)
  
  if (nrow(cov_coefs) == 0) return(0)  # unadjusted model
  
  # compute pooled covariate means across imputations (3+ families, excl 2017)
  cov_names_in_data <- c("age", "sex", "ethn_binary", "ukborn", "urban", 
                         "edu_qual", "marstat", "equiv_yearly", "oc_current", "chron_health")
  
  cov_means <- imp_data_long %>%
    filter(.imp > 0, family_3plus == 1, !(family_3plus == 1 & third_child_yob == 2017)) %>%
    summarise(across(all_of(cov_names_in_data), ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "term", values_to = "mean_val")
  
  # match coefficient names to covariate means and compute contribution
  # (for factor variables this is approximate but standard practice for marginal means)
  contribution <- cov_coefs %>%
    left_join(cov_means, by = "term") %>%
    mutate(contrib = ifelse(!is.na(mean_val), estimate * mean_val, 0)) %>%
    pull(contrib) %>%
    sum(na.rm = TRUE)
  
  contribution
}

# helper: make ITS panel with predicted marginal means
make_its_panel <- function(plot_data, pooled_model, outcome_label, outcome_ylab, imp_data_long) {
  
  # extract ITS coefficients
  coefs <- summary(pooled_model) %>% select(term, estimate)
  b0 <- coefs$estimate[coefs$term == "(Intercept)"]
  b1 <- coefs$estimate[coefs$term == "time_since_policy"]
  b2 <- coefs$estimate[coefs$term == "post_policy_month"]
  b3 <- coefs$estimate[coefs$term == "time_since_policy:post_policy_month"]
  
  # covariate contribution at means (for adjusted models)
  cov_offset <- compute_covariate_contribution(pooled_model, imp_data_long)
  
  yr_min <- min(plot_data$intyear)
  yr_max <- max(plot_data$intyear)
  
  # time_since_policy = intyear - 2017
  # predicted marginal mean: b0 + b1*t + b2*post + b3*t*post + cov_offset
  
  # pre-policy fitted line
  pre_years  <- seq(yr_min, 2016)
  pre_t      <- pre_years - 2017
  pre_fitted <- data.frame(
    year = pre_years, 
    y    = b0 + b1 * pre_t + cov_offset
  )
  
  # post-policy actual fitted line
  post_years  <- seq(2018, yr_max)
  post_t      <- post_years - 2017
  post_fitted <- data.frame(
    year = post_years, 
    y    = b0 + b1 * post_t + b2 + b3 * post_t + cov_offset
  )
  
  # counterfactual: pre-policy slope extended forward
  counterfact <- data.frame(
    year = post_years, 
    y    = b0 + b1 * post_t + cov_offset
  )
  
  ggplot() +
    # observed means as transparent dots
    geom_point(data = plot_data,
               aes(x = intyear, y = pooled_mean),
               colour = "#0072B2", size = 2.5, alpha = 0.3) +
    # pre-policy fitted line
    geom_line(data = pre_fitted,
              aes(x = year, y = y),
              colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 1.1) +
    # post-policy actual fitted line
    geom_line(data = post_fitted,
              aes(x = year, y = y),
              colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 1.1) +
    # counterfactual
    geom_line(data = counterfact,
              aes(x = year, y = y),
              colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "22") +
    # policy line
    geom_vline(xintercept = 2017, colour = "#D55E00",
               linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(yr_min, yr_max, by = 2)) +
    labs(title = outcome_label, x = "", y = outcome_ylab) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
      axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
}

# list of adjusted pooled model objects (unchanged)
its_adj_pooled_models <- list(
  pooled_its_GHQ_full_adj,
  pooled_its_SF_full_adj,
  pooled_its_general_health_full_adj,
  pooled_its_health_sat_full_adj,
  pooled_its_life_sat_full_adj,
  pooled_its_finnow_full_adj,
  pooled_its_finfut_full_adj
)

# build plot data for all 7 outcomes
its_plot_data_all <- map(outcomes_raw, ~build_its_plot_data(.x, imp_long_no2017))

# generate individual panels with figure labels
its_panels <- pmap(list(seq_along(outcomes_raw), outcome_labels_figures, outcome_ylabs_figures), function(j, label, ylab) {
  make_its_panel(its_plot_data_all[[j]], its_adj_pooled_models[[j]], label, ylab, imp_long_no2017)
})

# reorder and assemble with legend as 8th panel
its_ordered <- its_panels[display_order]

# create a dummy plot for the ITS legend
its_legend_source <- ggplot() +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 1.5, colour = "Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)"), linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(x = 1, y = 1, colour = "Observed mean"), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(x = c(1, 2), y = c(1, 2), colour = "Fitted trend"), linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_line(aes(x = c(1, 2), y = c(1, 1.5), colour = "Counterfactual"), linewidth = 0.7, linetype = "22") +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = "",
    values = c("Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)" = "#D55E00",
               "Observed mean" = "#0072B2", "Fitted trend" = "#0072B2",
               "Counterfactual" = "#0072B2"),
    breaks = c("Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)", "Observed mean", "Fitted trend", "Counterfactual"),
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(
      shape    = c(NA, 16, NA, NA),
      linetype = c("dashed", "blank", "solid", "22"),
      linewidth = c(0.8, NA, 1.1, 0.7),
      alpha    = c(1, 0.3, 1, 1)
    ))
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "center", legend.text = element_text(size = 8))

its_legend_panel <- make_legend_panel(its_legend_source)

its_combined <- (its_ordered[[1]] | its_ordered[[2]] | its_ordered[[3]] | its_ordered[[4]]) /
  (its_ordered[[5]] | its_ordered[[6]] | its_ordered[[7]] | its_legend_panel) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Changes in parental outcomes over time following the two-child benefit cap implementation",
    subtitle = "Marginal means shown. Higher scores indicate worse outcomes.",
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9)
    )
  )

pdf("output/ITS_all_outcomes_multipanel_20260330.pdf", width = 16, height = 9)
print(its_combined)
dev.off()
```

This code chunk also does the following for standardised adjusted figures.

```{r}
#| label: its-adjusted
## ITS Z-SCORE FIGURE — predicted marginal means, z-scored outcomes ----

# list of z-score adjusted pooled model objects
its_adj_z_pooled_models <- list(
  pooled_its_GHQ_full_adj_z,
  pooled_its_SF_full_adj_z,
  pooled_its_general_health_full_adj_z,
  pooled_its_health_sat_full_adj_z,
  pooled_its_life_sat_full_adj_z,
  pooled_its_finnow_full_adj_z,
  pooled_its_finfut_full_adj_z
)

# build z-scored plot data
its_plot_data_all_z <- map(outcomes_z_names, ~build_its_plot_data(.x, imp_long_no2017))

# auto-calculate shared symmetric y-axis range across all z-scored ITS panels
its_z_all_means <- unlist(map(its_plot_data_all_z, ~.x$pooled_mean))
its_z_ylim <- c(min(its_z_all_means, na.rm = TRUE) - 0.15, max(its_z_all_means, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.15)
its_z_ylim <- c(-max(abs(its_z_ylim)), max(abs(its_z_ylim)))

# helper: make ITS panel with predicted marginal means (z-score version, shared y-axis)
make_its_panel_z <- function(plot_data, pooled_model, outcome_label, outcome_ylab, imp_data_long, shared_ylim) {
  
  # extract ITS coefficients
  coefs <- summary(pooled_model) %>% select(term, estimate)
  b0 <- coefs$estimate[coefs$term == "(Intercept)"]
  b1 <- coefs$estimate[coefs$term == "time_since_policy"]
  b2 <- coefs$estimate[coefs$term == "post_policy_month"]
  b3 <- coefs$estimate[coefs$term == "time_since_policy:post_policy_month"]
  
  # covariate contribution at means (for adjusted models)
  cov_offset <- compute_covariate_contribution(pooled_model, imp_data_long)
  
  yr_min <- min(plot_data$intyear)
  yr_max <- max(plot_data$intyear)
  
  # pre-policy fitted line
  pre_years  <- seq(yr_min, 2016)
  pre_t      <- pre_years - 2017
  pre_fitted <- data.frame(year = pre_years, y = b0 + b1 * pre_t + cov_offset)
  
  # post-policy actual fitted line
  post_years  <- seq(2018, yr_max)
  post_t      <- post_years - 2017
  post_fitted <- data.frame(year = post_years, y = b0 + b1 * post_t + b2 + b3 * post_t + cov_offset)
  
  # counterfactual: pre-policy slope extended forward
  counterfact <- data.frame(year = post_years, y = b0 + b1 * post_t + cov_offset)
  
  ggplot() +
    # zero reference line
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dotted") +
    # observed means as transparent dots
    geom_point(data = plot_data,
               aes(x = intyear, y = pooled_mean),
               colour = "#0072B2", size = 2.5, alpha = 0.3) +
    # pre-policy fitted line
    geom_line(data = pre_fitted,
              aes(x = year, y = y),
              colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 1.1) +
    # post-policy actual fitted line
    geom_line(data = post_fitted,
              aes(x = year, y = y),
              colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 1.1) +
    # counterfactual
    geom_line(data = counterfact,
              aes(x = year, y = y),
              colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "22") +
    # policy line
    geom_vline(xintercept = 2017, colour = "#D55E00",
               linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(yr_min, yr_max, by = 2)) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = shared_ylim) +
    labs(title = outcome_label, x = "", y = outcome_ylab) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
      axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
}

# generate z-score ITS panels
its_panels_z <- pmap(list(seq_along(outcomes_raw), outcome_labels_figures, outcome_ylabs_figures), function(j, label, ylab) {
  make_its_panel_z(its_plot_data_all_z[[j]], its_adj_z_pooled_models[[j]], label, ylab, imp_long_no2017, its_z_ylim)
})

# reorder and assemble with legend as 8th panel
its_ordered_z <- its_panels_z[display_order]

its_combined_z <- (its_ordered_z[[1]] | its_ordered_z[[2]] | its_ordered_z[[3]] | its_ordered_z[[4]]) /
  (its_ordered_z[[5]] | its_ordered_z[[6]] | its_ordered_z[[7]] | its_legend_panel) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Changes in parental outcomes over time following the two-child benefit cap implementation",
    subtitle = "Marginal means on standardised scale from interrupted time series models shown. Higher scores indicate worse outcomes.",
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9)
    )
  )

pdf("output/ITS_all_outcomes_multipanel_zscore_20260330.pdf", width = 16, height = 9)
print(its_combined_z)
dev.off()

# also save individual outcome PDFs
walk2(its_panels, outcome_labels_figures, function(p, label) {
  safe_label <- gsub("[^a-zA-Z0-9]", "_", label)
  pdf(paste0("output/ITS_", safe_label, "_plot.pdf"), width = 10, height = 6)
  print(p)
  dev.off()
})
```

#### Generating tables

Then, the following chunk of code creates an ITS results workbook,
containing the following:

-   unadjusted raw results

-   adjusted raw results

-   standardised adjusted results

-   subgroup analyses (sex)

-   subgroup analyses (ethnicity)

-   subgroup analyses (income quintiles)

-   a formatted summary table of 1-3, including coefficients, 90% CIs,
    and significance stars for the full analyses

-   a formatted summary table of 4-6 for each group, including
    coefficients, 90% CIs, and significance stars for each subgroup

The last two bullet points here will be what goes into the tables for
the manuscript/supplement.

NB that this code export also uses the old labelling for outcomes, so
can use the above information in "Setup" for the most up-to-date
labelling.

```{r}
#| label: its-excel-export
## ITS Excel export
# create workbook for ITS results
wb_its <- createWorkbook()

# unadjusted (raw) - CORRECTED
addWorksheet(wb_its, "ITS_Full_Unadj")
its_tab_unadj <- bind_rows(
  summary(its_GHQ_full_unadj_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Ghq Total"),
  summary(its_SF_full_unadj_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Sf Total"),
  summary(its_general_health_full_unadj_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "General Health"),
  summary(its_health_sat_full_unadj_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Health Sat"),
  summary(its_life_sat_full_unadj_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Life Sat"),
  summary(its_finnow_full_unadj_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Finnow"),
  summary(its_finfut_full_unadj_pooled, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Finfut")
)
writeData(wb_its, "ITS_Full_Unadj", its_tab_unadj)

# adjusted (raw)
addWorksheet(wb_its, "ITS_Full_Adj")
its_tab_adj <- bind_rows(
  summary(pooled_its_GHQ_full_adj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Ghq Total"),
  summary(pooled_its_SF_full_adj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Sf Total"),
  summary(pooled_its_general_health_full_adj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "General Health"),
  summary(pooled_its_health_sat_full_adj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Health Sat"),
  summary(pooled_its_life_sat_full_adj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Life Sat"),
  summary(pooled_its_finnow_full_adj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Finnow"),
  summary(pooled_its_finfut_full_adj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Finfut")
) %>%
  filter(!grepl("age|sex|ethn_binary|ukborn|urban|edu_qual|marstat|equiv_yearly|oc_current|chron_health", term))
writeData(wb_its, "ITS_Full_Adj", its_tab_adj)

# adjusted (z-scored)
addWorksheet(wb_its, "ITS_Full_Adj_Z")
its_tab_adj_z <- bind_rows(
  summary(pooled_its_GHQ_full_adj_z, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Ghq Total (standardised)"),
  summary(pooled_its_SF_full_adj_z, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Sf Total (standardised)"),
  summary(pooled_its_general_health_full_adj_z, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "General Health (standardised)"),
  summary(pooled_its_health_sat_full_adj_z, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Health Sat (standardised)"),
  summary(pooled_its_life_sat_full_adj_z, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Life Sat (standardised)"),
  summary(pooled_its_finnow_full_adj_z, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Finnow (standardised)"),
  summary(pooled_its_finfut_full_adj_z, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Finfut (standardised)")
) %>%
  filter(!grepl("age|sex|ethn_binary|ukborn|urban|edu_qual|marstat|equiv_yearly|oc_current|chron_health", term))
writeData(wb_its, "ITS_Full_Adj_Z", its_tab_adj_z)

# subgroup analyses - sex
addWorksheet(wb_its, "ITS_Subgroup_Sex")
its_subgroup_sex <- bind_rows(
  summary(pooled_its_GHQ_male_adj_z, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Ghq Total (standardised)", subgroup = "Male"),
  summary(pooled_its_GHQ_female_adj_z, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Ghq Total (standardised)", subgroup = "Female"),
```

## Difference-in-differences (DiD) analyses

This paper actually uses two methods of difference-in-differences
analysis. The two methods for this are:

-   DiD with propensity score matching (DiD + PSM)

-   a classic DiD using 2016 as the "before" timepoint and 2023 as the
    "after" time point, as by then, all 3+ children families included in
    the study would have been affected by the policy

However, before either DiD (or CITS, later on) are run, the parallel
trends assumption needs to be tested.

### Parallel trends assumption testing

In essence, what this means is that we need to check whether both 3+
children (affected) and 1-2 children (control) groups were moving in the
same direction between two time points before the implementation,
otherwise it can be hard to parse out whether the change seen (if any)
after the implementation in the affected group is because of the policy.

#### Visual parallel trends testing

Even though we'll test it numerically, it makes sense to have a visual
representation of this as well, as it'll be helpful to once again
compare across outcomes and we'll have a better idea of what these
numbers mean.

For this, I'll specifically be comparing time periods 1 (2009-2012) and
2 (2013-2016) and generating a parallel trends figure using the
standardised adjusted scoring (shared y-axis, 0 midpoint).

With this figure, as well as with all the other figures generated
onwards, I'll be using the same workflow/setup as the ITS-generated
figures in terms of pooling results and generating a multipanel figure
including each outcome, with the 8th panel being the legend.

Visually, if the lines are regressing towards the mean, then that may be
an indication that the parallel trends assumption could be violated.

##### Figure generation

```{r}
#| label: build-parallel-trends-plot-data-pooled-m
# build parallel trends plot data: pooled means and 90% CIs by time_bucket and group, z-scored outcomes
pt_data_all <- map(outcomes_z_names, function(ov) {
  imp_summaries <- lapply(1:imp_pt$m, function(i) {
    complete(imp_pt, i) %>%
      mutate(group = case_when(
        family_3plus == 0 ~ "Control (1-2 children)",
        family_3plus == 1 ~ "Treatment (3+ children)",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      )) %>%
      filter(!is.na(group)) %>%
      group_by(time_bucket, group) %>%
      summarise(
        mean_val = mean(.data[[ov]], na.rm = TRUE),
        sd_val   = sd(.data[[ov]], na.rm = TRUE),
        n        = n(),
        .groups  = "drop"
      ) %>%
      mutate(.imp = i)
  })
```

```{r}
#| label: parallel-trends-z-score-figure-shared-y
  bind_rows(imp_summaries) %>%
    group_by(time_bucket, group) %>%
    summarise(
      pooled_mean = mean(mean_val),
      pooled_sd   = sqrt(mean(sd_val^2) + var(mean_val) * (1 + 1/20)),
      pooled_n    = mean(n),
      pooled_se   = pooled_sd / sqrt(pooled_n),
      ci_lower    = pooled_mean - 1.645 * pooled_se,
      ci_upper    = pooled_mean + 1.645 * pooled_se,
      .groups     = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(outcome = ov)
})
```

```{r}
#| label: auto-calculate-shared-symmetric-y-axis-r-2
# auto-calculate shared symmetric y-axis range across all z-scored PT panels
# uses CI bounds (not just means) so error bars aren't clipped
pt_z_all_ci <- c(unlist(map(pt_data_all, ~.x$ci_lower)), unlist(map(pt_data_all, ~.x$ci_upper)))
pt_z_ylim <- c(min(pt_z_all_ci, na.rm = TRUE) - 0.05, max(pt_z_all_ci, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.05)
# make symmetric around 0
pt_z_ylim <- c(-max(abs(pt_z_ylim)), max(abs(pt_z_ylim)))
```

```{r}
#| label: parallel-trends-z-score-figure-shared-y-2
pt_panels_z <- pmap(list(pt_data_all, outcome_labels_figures, outcome_ylabs_figures), function(dat, label, ylab) {
  ggplot(dat, aes(x = time_bucket, y = pooled_mean, color = group, shape = group)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper), width = 0.08, linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2),
                       labels = c("2009-2012", "2013-2016")) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"   = "#E69F00",
      "Treatment (3+ children)"  = "#0072B2"
    ), labels = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"   = "1-2 children (control)",
      "Treatment (3+ children)"  = "3+ children"
    )) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"   = 16,
      "Treatment (3+ children)"  = 15
    ), labels = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"   = "1-2 children (control)",
      "Treatment (3+ children)"  = "3+ children"
    )) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = pt_z_ylim) +
    labs(title = label, x = "", y = ylab,
         color = "Group", shape = "Group") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
      legend.position  = "none",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
})
```

```{r}
#| label: reorder-and-assemble-with-legend-as-8th-4
# reorder and assemble with legend as 8th panel
pt_ordered_z <- pt_panels_z[display_order]
```

```{r}
#| label: custom-parallel-trends-legend-with-consi
# custom parallel trends legend with consistent order
pt_legend_source <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(aes(x = 1, y = 1, colour = "3+ children"), size = 3, shape = 15) +
  geom_point(aes(x = 1, y = 1, colour = "1-2 children (control)"), size = 3, shape = 16) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = "",
    values = c("3+ children" = "#0072B2",
               "1-2 children (control)" = "#E69F00"),
    breaks = c("3+ children", "1-2 children (control)"),
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(
      shape = c(15, 16)
    ))
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "center", legend.text = element_text(size = 8))
```

```{r}
#| label: parallel-trends-z-score-figure-shared-y-3
pt_legend_z <- make_legend_panel(pt_legend_source)
```

```{r}
#| label: parallel-trends-z-score-figure-shared-y-4
pt_combined_z <- (pt_ordered_z[[1]] | pt_ordered_z[[2]] | pt_ordered_z[[3]] | pt_ordered_z[[4]]) /
  (pt_ordered_z[[5]] | pt_ordered_z[[6]] | pt_ordered_z[[7]] | pt_legend_z) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Parallel Trends Test: All Outcomes (standardised)",
    subtitle = "Marginal means on standardised scale shown. Pre-policy periods only (2009-2012, 2013-2016). Higher scores indicate worse outcomes.",
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8)
    )
  )
```

##### Exporting results

```{r}
pdf("output/parallel_trends_all_outcomes_multipanel_zscore_20260330.pdf", width = 16, height = 9)
print(pt_combined_z)
dev.off()
```

#### Numerical parallel trends testing

For the numerical tests, the parallel trends assumption is testing the
interaction between `time_bucket` (the variable indicating either time
period 1 or 2) and `family_3plus` (the binary indicator of whether an
individual has either 3+ children or 1-2 children). If the interaction
is significant, the parallel trends assumption is violated. I test this
for unadjusted (raw), adjusted (raw), and standardised adjusted models
for each outcome, before then generating an Excel workbook with all the
results (same workflow for ITS, which I adapt for all subsequent
numerical models too).

##### Unadjusted (raw) parallel trends

**Psychological distress**
```{r}
#| label: ghq-total-3
# GHQ_total
parallel_trends_GHQ <- lapply(1:imp_pt$m, function(i) {
  feols(GHQ_total ~ time_bucket * family_3plus,
        data = complete(imp_pt, i),
        cluster = ~hidp)
})
class(parallel_trends_GHQ) <- c("mira", "list")
pooled_parallel_GHQ <- pool(parallel_trends_GHQ)
summary(pooled_parallel_GHQ, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90)
```

### Difference-in-differences analysis with propensity score matching (DiD + PSM)

#### Matching procedure

In order to keep the before-and-after groups for 3+ children as similar
as possible, we wanted to match each individual from the affected
post-policy group to an individual with 1) the same number of children,
3) whose youngest child is the same age.

Matching will be done for both time periods 1-3 and 2-3 in order to
create a visual representation of time trends, although the DiD+PSM
analysis will only use time periods 2 (pre) and 3 (post) as these are
the most proximal to each other.

Here, I've commented out the matching command, but this is what you
would run in order to match individuals from time periods 2 and 3. You
can instead just pre-load the matched `mids` object.

```{r}

# imp_3plus_23 <- as.mids(imp_long_3plus_23)

# matched_imp_23 <- matchthem(
#   I(time_bucket == 3) ~ age_youngest_child + n_children_5_under,
#   datasets = imp_3plus_23,
#   approach = "within",
#   method = "optimal",
#   ratio = 1,
#   distance = "glm"
# )
# summary(matched_imp_23)
# saveRDS(matched_imp_23, "UKHLS_imputation_matched_23_20260310.rds")
matched_imp_23 <- readRDS("UKHLS_imputation_matched_23_20260310.rds")
```

#### Updated power analysis for DiD + PSM (matched sample)

Because there are a different number of individuals included in the 3+
children group (only individuals post-policy and their matched
pre-policy counterparts), power calculations need to be rerun with the
updated Ns. I do this here below, as well as adding a sheet with the
updated results to the existing power analysis Excel sheet (so now, this
saves as the most recent version).

```{r}
#| label: did-power-analysis
did_matched_ns <- map_dfr(seq_along(outcomes_raw), function(j) {
  outcome <- outcomes_raw[j]
  label   <- outcome_labels[j]
  
  matched_n_trt <- mean(sapply(1:imp_3plus_23$m, function(i) {
    nrow(MatchIt::match.data(matched_imp_23$models[[i]]))
  }))
  
  matched_n_ctrl <- mean(sapply(1:imp_no2017$m, function(i) {
    complete(imp_no2017, i) %>%
      filter(family_3plus == 0, time_bucket %in% c(2, 3)) %>%
      nrow()
  }))
  
  pd <- compute_power_stats(outcome, imp_long_no2017 %>% filter(time_bucket %in% c(2, 3)))
  p_sd <- mean(pd$pooled_sd)
  
  did_05 <- pwr.t2n.test(n1 = matched_n_trt, n2 = matched_n_ctrl, power = 0.80, sig.level = 0.05)
  did_10 <- pwr.t2n.test(n1 = matched_n_trt, n2 = matched_n_ctrl, power = 0.80, sig.level = 0.10)
  
  data.frame(
    Outcome     = label,
    Analysis    = "DiD (matched)",
    Alpha       = c(0.05, 0.10),
    Power       = 0.80,
    N_Treatment = matched_n_trt,
    N_Control   = matched_n_ctrl,
    Pooled_SD   = p_sd,
    MDE_Cohen_d = c(did_05$d, did_10$d),
    MDE_Raw     = c(did_05$d, did_10$d) * p_sd
  )
})

# exporting results
addWorksheet(wb_power, "Power_DiD_Matched")
writeData(wb_power, "Power_DiD_Matched", did_matched_ns)
saveWorkbook(wb_power, "output/Power_Analysis_20260320.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

#### DiD + PSM full models

For all of these full models, this uses the same structure as the ITS
models, where full models (unadjusted raw / adjusted raw / standardised
adjusted), as well as standardised adjusted subgroup models are run for
each outcome.

As done above, all models are pooled across the 20 imputed matched
datasets.

##### Unadjusted (raw)

**Psychological distress**
```{r}
#| label: ghq-total-unadjusted
# GHQ_total unadjusted
did_GHQ_full_unadj <- lapply(1:imp_3plus_23$m, function(i) {
  matched_data <- MatchIt::match.data(matched_imp_23$models[[i]]) %>%
    select(-weights, -subclass, -distance)
  control_data <- complete(imp_no2017, i) %>%
    filter(family_3plus == 0, time_bucket %in% c(2, 3))
  analysis_data <- rbind(matched_data, control_data)
  feols(GHQ_total ~ family_3plus * I(time_bucket == 3),
        data = analysis_data,
        cluster = ~hidp)
})
class(did_GHQ_full_unadj) <- c("mira", "list")
pooled_did_GHQ_full_unadj <- pool(did_GHQ_full_unadj)
summary(pooled_did_GHQ_full_unadj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90)
```

#### DiD + PSM subgroup analyses

This section did it a bit different to avoid writing out the matched
data extraction pipeline each time (with ITS, I could use the original
model construction and just run it on subgroups - although a helper
function could theoretically have been used - but then with the DiD
here, because of the extraction of each matched pair and combining it
with the control group, it would added hundreds more lines to do it
individually).

##### Helper functions

```{r}
#| label: helper-to-build-matched-control-analysis
# helper to build matched+control analysis data for subgroups
build_did_data <- function(i, subgroup_filter = NULL) {
  matched_data <- MatchIt::match.data(matched_imp_23$models[[i]]) %>%
    select(-weights, -subclass, -distance)
  control_data <- complete(imp_no2017, i) %>%
    filter(family_3plus == 0, time_bucket %in% c(2, 3))
  analysis_data <- rbind(matched_data, control_data)
  if (!is.null(subgroup_filter)) {
    analysis_data <- analysis_data %>% filter(!!subgroup_filter)
  }
  analysis_data
}

# helper to run a DiD subgroup model
run_did_subgroup <- function(outcome_z, subgroup_expr, covariates) {
  f <- as.formula(paste0(outcome_z, " ~ family_3plus * I(time_bucket == 3) + ", covariates))
  model_list <- lapply(1:imp_3plus_23$m, function(i) {
    ad <- build_did_data(i, subgroup_expr)
    feols(f, data = ad, cluster = ~hidp)
  })
  class(model_list) <- c("mira", "list")
  pool(model_list)
}

# covariate strings (without the stratifying variable)
covs_no_sex  <- "age + ethn_binary + ukborn + urban + edu_qual + marstat + equiv_yearly + oc_current + chron_health"
covs_no_ethn <- "age + sex + ukborn + urban + edu_qual + marstat + equiv_yearly + oc_current + chron_health"
covs_no_inc  <- "age + sex + ethn_binary + ukborn + urban + edu_qual + marstat + oc_current + chron_health"

# z-scored outcome names
outcomes_z <- paste0(outcomes_raw, "_z")
```

##### Sex subgroups

###### Male
```{r}
#| label: male-sex-1-2
# male (sex == 1)
did_male_results <- map(outcomes_z, ~run_did_subgroup(.x, expr(sex == 1), covs_no_sex))
names(did_male_results) <- outcomes_z
pooled_did_GHQ_male_adj_z            <- did_male_results[["GHQ_total_z"]]
pooled_did_SF_male_adj_z             <- did_male_results[["SF_total_z"]]
pooled_did_general_health_male_adj_z <- did_male_results[["general_health_z"]]
pooled_did_health_sat_male_adj_z     <- did_male_results[["health_sat_z"]]
pooled_did_life_sat_male_adj_z       <- did_male_results[["life_sat_z"]]
pooled_did_finnow_male_adj_z         <- did_male_results[["finnow_z"]]
pooled_did_finfut_male_adj_z         <- did_male_results[["finfut_z"]]
```

#### Data exporting and figure generation

This code first contains a series of chunks used to generate various
figures from the data, and then several chunks used to create an Excel
workbook with numerical results.

Note that the figures (the raw and standardised ones, respectively) are
being built with the end goal of having the two DiD versions (DiD + PSM
and Classic 2016-2023) appended into one figure, and the panel labelling
will therefore reflect that - if you're wanting to generate separate
DiD/PSM and Classic DiD figures that have no reference to each other,
that specific line can be commented out/removed.

First, I construct the raw-outcome DiD plots.

```{r}
#| label: build-did-plot-data-pooled-means-and-90
## build DiD plot data: pooled means and 90% CIs by time_bucket and group, raw outcomes
did_plot_data_all <- map(outcomes_raw, function(ov) {
  imp_summaries <- lapply(1:imp_3plus_23$m, function(i) {
    matched_data_23 <- MatchIt::match.data(matched_imp_23$models[[i]]) %>%
      select(-weights, -subclass, -distance)
    matched_data_13 <- MatchIt::match.data(matched_imp_13$models[[i]]) %>%
      select(-weights, -subclass, -distance) %>%
      filter(time_bucket == 1)
    control_data <- complete(imp_no2017, i) %>%
      filter(family_3plus == 0, time_bucket %in% c(1, 2, 3))
    
    combined <- rbind(matched_data_13, matched_data_23, control_data) %>%
      mutate(group = case_when(
        family_3plus == 0  ~ "Control (1-2 children)",
        family_3plus == 1  ~ "3+ (matched)",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      )) %>%
      filter(!is.na(group)) %>%
      group_by(time_bucket, group) %>%
      summarise(
        mean_val = mean(.data[[ov]], na.rm = TRUE),
        sd_val   = sd(.data[[ov]], na.rm = TRUE),
        n        = n(),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      mutate(.imp = i)
    
    rm(matched_data_23, matched_data_13, control_data)
    gc()
    
    combined
  })
  
  bind_rows(imp_summaries) %>%
    group_by(time_bucket, group) %>%
    summarise(
      pooled_mean = mean(mean_val),
      pooled_sd   = sqrt(mean(sd_val^2) + var(mean_val) * (1 + 1/20)),
      pooled_n    = mean(n),
      pooled_se   = pooled_sd / sqrt(pooled_n),
      ci_lower    = pooled_mean - 1.645 * pooled_se,
      ci_upper    = pooled_mean + 1.645 * pooled_se,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(outcome = ov)
})

did_panels <- pmap(list(did_plot_data_all, outcome_labels_figures, outcome_ylabs_figures), function(dat, label, ylab) {
  dat_filtered <- dat %>% filter(time_bucket %in% c(2, 3))
  ggplot(dat_filtered, aes(x = as.factor(time_bucket), y = pooled_mean,
                           colour = group, shape = group)) +
    # policy line
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper),
                  width = 0.1, linewidth = 0.8,
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)" = "#E69F00",
      "3+ (matched)"           = "#0072B2"
    ), labels = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)" = "1-2 children (control)",
      "3+ (matched)"           = "3+ children (matched)"
    )) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)" = 16,
      "3+ (matched)"           = 15
    ), labels = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)" = "1-2 children (control)",
      "3+ (matched)"           = "3+ children (matched)"
    )) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = c(
      "2" = "Pre-policy\n(2013-2016)",
      "3" = "Post-policy\n(2018-2023)"
    )) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 5)) +
    labs(title = label, x = "", y = ylab,
         colour = "Group", shape = "Group") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
      legend.position  = "none",
      axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 7),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
})

# custom DiD legend with policy line and consistent order
did_legend_source <- ggplot() +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 1.5, colour = "Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)"), linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(x = 1, y = 1, colour = "3+ children (matched)"), size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = 1, y = 1, colour = "1-2 children (control)"), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = "",
    values = c("Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)" = "#D55E00",
               "3+ children (matched)" = "#0072B2",
               "1-2 children (control)" = "#E69F00"),
    breaks = c("Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)", "3+ children (matched)", "1-2 children (control)"),
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(
      shape    = c(NA, 15, 16),
      linetype = c("dashed", "blank", "blank"),
      linewidth = c(0.8, NA, NA)
    ))
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "center", legend.text = element_text(size = 8))

did_legend   <- make_legend_panel(did_legend_source)
did_legend_z <- did_legend

# reorder and assemble with legend as 8th panel
did_ordered <- did_panels[display_order]

did_combined <- (did_ordered[[1]] | did_ordered[[2]] | did_ordered[[3]] | did_ordered[[4]]) /
  (did_ordered[[5]] | did_ordered[[6]] | did_ordered[[7]] | did_legend) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Relative change in parental outcomes pre-post the two-child benefit cap for those with 3+ children compared to 1-2 children",
    subtitle = "Panel A: PSM-matched DiD.\nMarginal means shown. Higher scores indicate worse outcomes.",
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8)
    )
  )

pdf("output/DiD_all_outcomes_multipanel_20260330.pdf", width = 16, height = 9)
print(did_combined)
dev.off()
```

Next is the figure with standardised adjusted outcomes (matched in all
periods, z-scored outcomes).

```{r}
#| label: build-z-scored-did-plot-data-same-matchi
# build z-scored DiD plot data (same matching structure as raw, but using _z outcomes)
did_plot_data_all_z <- map(outcomes_z_names, function(ov) {
  imp_summaries <- lapply(1:imp_3plus_23$m, function(i) {
    matched_data_23 <- MatchIt::match.data(matched_imp_23$models[[i]]) %>%
      select(-weights, -subclass, -distance)
    matched_data_13 <- MatchIt::match.data(matched_imp_13$models[[i]]) %>%
      select(-weights, -subclass, -distance) %>%
      filter(time_bucket == 1)
    control_data <- complete(imp_no2017, i) %>%
      filter(family_3plus == 0, time_bucket %in% c(1, 2, 3))
    
    combined <- rbind(matched_data_13, matched_data_23, control_data) %>%
      mutate(group = case_when(
        family_3plus == 0  ~ "Control (1-2 children)",
        family_3plus == 1  ~ "3+ (matched)",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      )) %>%
      filter(!is.na(group)) %>%
      group_by(time_bucket, group) %>%
      summarise(
        mean_val = mean(.data[[ov]], na.rm = TRUE),
        sd_val   = sd(.data[[ov]], na.rm = TRUE),
        n        = n(),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      mutate(.imp = i)
    
    rm(matched_data_23, matched_data_13, control_data)
    gc()
    
    combined
  })
  
  bind_rows(imp_summaries) %>%
    group_by(time_bucket, group) %>%
    summarise(
      pooled_mean = mean(mean_val),
      pooled_sd   = sqrt(mean(sd_val^2) + var(mean_val) * (1 + 1/20)),
      pooled_n    = mean(n),
      pooled_se   = pooled_sd / sqrt(pooled_n),
      ci_lower    = pooled_mean - 1.645 * pooled_se,
      ci_upper    = pooled_mean + 1.645 * pooled_se,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(outcome = ov)
})

# auto-calculate shared symmetric y-axis range across all z-scored DiD panels
did_z_all_ci <- c(unlist(map(did_plot_data_all_z, ~.x$ci_lower)),
                  unlist(map(did_plot_data_all_z, ~.x$ci_upper)))
did_z_ylim <- c(min(did_z_all_ci, na.rm = TRUE) - 0.05, max(did_z_all_ci, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.05)
did_z_ylim <- c(-max(abs(did_z_ylim)), max(abs(did_z_ylim)))

did_panels_z <- pmap(list(did_plot_data_all_z, outcome_labels_figures, outcome_ylabs_figures), function(dat, label, ylab) {
  dat_filtered <- dat %>% filter(time_bucket %in% c(2, 3))
  ggplot(dat_filtered, aes(x = as.factor(time_bucket), y = pooled_mean,
                           colour = group, shape = group)) +
    # policy line
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 0.8) +
    # zero reference line
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper),
                  width = 0.1, linewidth = 0.8,
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)" = "#E69F00",
      "3+ (matched)"           = "#0072B2"
    ), labels = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)" = "1-2 children (control)",
      "3+ (matched)"           = "3+ children (matched)"
    )) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)" = 16,
      "3+ (matched)"           = 15
    ), labels = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)" = "1-2 children (control)",
      "3+ (matched)"           = "3+ children (matched)"
    )) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = c(
      "2" = "Pre-policy\n(2013-2016)",
      "3" = "Post-policy\n(2018-2023)"
    )) +
    # shared y-axis across all panels, symmetric around 0
    coord_cartesian(ylim = did_z_ylim) +
    labs(title = label, x = "", y = ylab,
         colour = "Group", shape = "Group") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
      legend.position  = "none",
      axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 7),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
})

# reorder and assemble with legend as 8th panel
did_ordered_z <- did_panels_z[display_order]

did_combined_z <- (did_ordered_z[[1]] | did_ordered_z[[2]] | did_ordered_z[[3]] | did_ordered_z[[4]]) /
  (did_ordered_z[[5]] | did_ordered_z[[6]] | did_ordered_z[[7]] | did_legend_z) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Relative change in parental outcomes pre-post the two-child benefit cap for those with 3+ children compared to 1-2 children",
    subtitle = "Panel A: PSM-matched DiD.\nMarginal means on standardised scale shown. Higher scores indicate worse outcomes.",
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8)
    )
  )

pdf("output/DiD_all_outcomes_multipanel_zscore_20260330.pdf", width = 16, height = 9)
print(did_combined_z)
dev.off()
```

Finally I am exporting the data into an Excel workbook, containing the
following sheets (following the ITS workflow):

-   unadjusted raw results

-   adjusted raw results

-   standardised adjusted results

-   subgroup analyses (sex)

-   subgroup analyses (ethnicity)

-   subgroup analyses (income quintiles)

-   a formatted summary table of 1-3, including coefficients, 90% CIs,
    and significance stars for the full analyses

-   a formatted summary table of 4-6 for each group, including
    coefficients, 90% CIs, and significance stars for each subgroup

The last two bullet points here will be what goes into the tables for
the manuscript/supplement.

```{r}
#| label: did-excel-export-1
wb_did <- createWorkbook()
```

```{r}
#| label: unadjusted-raw
# unadjusted (raw)
addWorksheet(wb_did, "DiD_Full_Unadj")
did_tab_unadj <- bind_rows(
  summary(pooled_did_GHQ_full_unadj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Ghq Total"),
  summary(pooled_did_SF_full_unadj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Sf Total"),
  summary(pooled_did_general_health_full_unadj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "General Health"),
  summary(pooled_did_health_sat_full_unadj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Health Sat"),
  summary(pooled_did_life_sat_full_unadj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Life Sat"),
  summary(pooled_did_finnow_full_unadj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Finnow"),
  summary(pooled_did_finfut_full_unadj, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.90) %>% mutate(outcome = "Finfut")
)
writeData(wb_did, "DiD_Full_Unadj", did_tab_unadj)
```

```{r}
writeData(wb_did, "DiD_Subgroup_Income", did_subgroup_income)
```

### Classic DiD analysis: 2016 vs 2023

As explained above, I also ran a classic DiD analysis. This one was a
bit more simple as I didn't need to implement matching at each step.
Also, since I already checked parallel trends above, we didn't need to
do that for this one too.

This used a variation of the helper function style implemented above in
the matched DiD.

#### Code setup and helper functions

First, I filtered to the two years used in the analysis here and ran the
helper functions, which will be called three times for each kind of
model (unadjusted raw, adjusted raw, and standardised adjusted).

```{r}
#| label: classic-did-sensitivity-analysis-2016-vs
imp_long_classic <- imp_long_no2017 %>%
  filter(intyear %in% c(2016, 2023))
imp_classic <- as.mids(imp_long_classic)
```

```{r}
#| label: classic-did-sensitivity-analysis-2016-vs-2
run_classic_did <- function(outcome_var, imp_obj, adjusted = FALSE, z_score = FALSE) {
  ov <- if (z_score) paste0(outcome_var, "_z") else outcome_var
  if (adjusted) {
    formula_str <- paste0(ov, " ~ family_3plus * I(intyear == 2023) + ",
                          "age + sex + ethn_binary + ukborn + urban + edu_qual + ",
                          "marstat + equiv_yearly + oc_current + chron_health")
  } else {
    formula_str <- paste0(ov, " ~ family_3plus * I(intyear == 2023)")
  }
  f <- as.formula(formula_str)
  model_list <- lapply(1:imp_obj$m, function(i) {
    feols(f, data = complete(imp_obj, i), cluster = ~hidp)
  })
  class(model_list) <- c("mira", "list")
  pool(model_list)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: classic-did-sensitivity-analysis-2016-vs-3
classic_did_unadj <- map(outcomes_raw, ~run_classic_did(.x, imp_classic, adjusted = FALSE, z_score = FALSE))
classic_did_adj   <- map(outcomes_raw, ~run_classic_did(.x, imp_classic, adjusted = TRUE,  z_score = FALSE))
classic_did_adj_z <- map(outcomes_raw, ~run_classic_did(.x, imp_classic, adjusted = TRUE,  z_score = TRUE))
```

```{r}
#| label: classic-did-sensitivity-analysis-2016-vs-4
names(classic_did_unadj) <- outcomes_raw
names(classic_did_adj)   <- outcomes_raw
names(classic_did_adj_z) <- outcomes_raw
```

```{r}
#| label: classic-did-sensitivity-analysis-2016-vs-5
classic_did_term <- "family_3plus:I(intyear == 2023)"
```

```{r}

  Outcome = outcome_labels,
  Unadjusted = sapply(classic_did_unadj, function(m) format_result(m, classic_did_term)),
  Adjusted = sapply(classic_did_adj, function(m) format_result(m, classic_did_term)),
  Z_score_adjusted = sapply(classic_did_adj_z, function(m) format_result(m, classic_did_term))
)
names(classic_did_table) <- c("Outcome",
                              "Unadjusted\nDiD estimate (90% CI)",
                              "Adjusted\nDiD estimate (90% CI)",
                              "Standardised adjusted\nDiD estimate (90% CI)")
classic_did_table <- classic_did_table[display_order, ]
```

#### Classic DiD figure generation

This section generates two DiD (2016-2023) plots, following the
multi-panel/multi-outcome layouts of above figures.

Note that, just as above, this figure is built with the end goal of
having the two DiD version appended into one figure, and the panel
labelling does reflect that - if you're wanting to generate two separate
figures, that specific line can be commented out/removed.

As above, there is a raw classic DiD plot and standardised version.

##### Raw classic DiD plot

```{r}
#| label: build-classic-did-plot-data-raw-outcomes
# build classic DiD plot data: raw outcomes
classic_did_plot_data_all <- map(outcomes_raw, function(ov) {
  imp_long_classic %>%
    filter(.imp > 0) %>%
    mutate(group = case_when(
      family_3plus == 0 ~ "Control (1-2 children)",
      family_3plus == 1 ~ "Treatment (3+ children)",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )) %>%
    filter(!is.na(group)) %>%
    group_by(.imp, intyear, group) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_val = mean(.data[[ov]], na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_val   = sd(.data[[ov]], na.rm = TRUE),
      n        = n(),
      .groups  = "drop"
    ) %>%
    group_by(intyear, group) %>%
    summarise(
      pooled_mean = mean(mean_val),
      pooled_sd   = sqrt(mean(sd_val^2) + var(mean_val) * (1 + 1/20)),
      pooled_n    = mean(n),
      pooled_se   = pooled_sd / sqrt(pooled_n),
      ci_lower    = pooled_mean - 1.645 * pooled_se,
      ci_upper    = pooled_mean + 1.645 * pooled_se,
      .groups     = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(outcome = ov)
})

classic_did_panels <- pmap(list(classic_did_plot_data_all, outcome_labels_figures, outcome_ylabs_figures), function(dat, label, ylab) {
  ggplot(dat, aes(x = as.factor(intyear), y = pooled_mean,
                  colour = group, shape = group)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper),
                  width = 0.1, linewidth = 0.8,
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"   = "#E69F00",
      "Treatment (3+ children)"  = "#0072B2"
    ), labels = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"   = "1-2 children (control)",
      "Treatment (3+ children)"  = "3+ children"
    )) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"   = 16,
      "Treatment (3+ children)"  = 15
    ), labels = c(
      "Control (1-2 children)"   = "1-2 children (control)",
      "Treatment (3+ children)"  = "3+ children"
    )) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 5)) +
    labs(title = label, x = "", y = ylab,
         colour = "Group", shape = "Group") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
      legend.position  = "none",
      axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 7),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
})

# custom classic DiD legend with policy line and consistent order
classic_did_legend_source <- ggplot() +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 1.5, colour = "Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)"), linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(x = 1, y = 1, colour = "3+ children"), size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = 1, y = 1, colour = "1-2 children (control)"), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = "",
    values = c("Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)" = "#D55E00",
               "3+ children" = "#0072B2",
               "1-2 children (control)" = "#E69F00"),
    breaks = c("Two-child benefit cap\nintroduction (2017)", "3+ children", "1-2 children (control)"),
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(
      shape    = c(NA, 15, 16),
      linetype = c("dashed", "blank", "blank"),
      linewidth = c(0.8, NA, NA)
    ))
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "center", legend.text = element_text(size = 8))

classic_did_legend   <- make_legend_panel(classic_did_legend_source)
classic_did_legend_z <- classic_did_legend

classic_did_ordered <- classic_did_panels[display_order]

classic_did_combined <- (classic_did_ordered[[1]] | classic_did_ordered[[2]] | classic_did_ordered[[3]] | classic_did_ordered[[4]]) /
  (classic_did_ordered[[5]] | classic_did_ordered[[6]] | classic_did_ordered[[7]] | classic_did_legend) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "",
    subtitle = "Panel B: Classic DiD (2016 vs 2023).\nMarginal means shown. Higher scores indicate worse outcomes.",
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8)
    )
  )

pdf("output/Classic_DiD_multipanel_20260330.pdf", width = 16, height = 9)
print(classic_did_combined)
dev.off()
```

```{r}
#| label: build-classic-did-plot-data-z-scored-out
```
